claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically has residual porosity and structural weaknesses.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of 2–5 vol% B4C into the ZrB2 powder before sintering.
Adding 2–5 vol% B4C can lower the required ZrB2 sintering temperature.
Adding 2–5 vol% B4C can improve ZrB2 densification and reduce residual porosity.
B4C-modified ZrB2 can be sintered under an inert atmosphere at approximately 2100–2200 °C.
Sintering at 2100–2200 °C with B4C promotes reactive liquid-phase sintering while limiting excessive grain growth.
B4C addition promotes transient liquid-phase formation during ZrB2 sintering.
Transient phases generated by B4C reactions enhance mass transport during sintering.
Enhanced mass transport caused by the transient phases promotes pore healing and enables full densification at lower temperature.
Lower porosity will reduce hole formation and improve microstructural integrity during prolonged exposure to a liquid plating bath.
B4C-enhanced specimens sintered at 2100–2200 °C will have mechanical strength similar to or better than conventional ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
B4C-enhanced specimens will exhibit fewer pores than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
B4C-enhanced specimens will undergo less degradation during long-term liquid plating bath exposure than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
Porosity in conventional ZrB2 causes failure during exposure to a liquid plating bath.
